headline: Core Morpho Blue contracts fully verified on Etherscan, immutable (no proxy), sourced from pinned GitHub tags, and audited by multiple tier-1 firms including Spearbit, OpenZeppelin, Certora, and ChainSecurity

findings.text: Morpho Blue core singleton (0xBBBBBbbBBb9cC5e90e3b3Af64bdAF62C37EEFFCb, Ethereum) is verified on Etherscan (abiSource='etherscan', verified=true) and is NOT a proxy (proxy=null per /api/contract/abi response). The contract is explicitly immutable. The Adaptive Curve IRM (0x870aC11D48B15DB9a138Cf899d20F13F79Ba00BC) and other periphery contracts (MetaMorpho factories, VaultV2Factory, etc.) are also listed with source code links pointing to pinned GitHub tags in the official deployed-addresses doc.

The official Morpho docs (llms-full.txt) explicitly map every deployed contract to its GitHub source repo and tag: Morpho Blue core → github.com/morpho-org/morpho-blue/tree/v1.0.0; Adaptive Curve IRM → morpho-blue-irm/tree/v1.0.0; MetaMorpho V1.1 → metamorpho-v1.1/tree/5a0717b2...; Bundler3 → bundler3/tree/82e44dd...; Vault V2 → vault-v2; Pre-liquidation factory → pre-liquidation/tree/16978c5.... Commit SHAs are pinned in the docs for peripheral contracts. V2 repo-to-explorer matching was not independently compiled in this run.

Audit coverage confirmed via official docs (llms-full.txt audit table): Morpho Blue V1 core audited by Spearbit (Oct 2023), OpenZeppelin (Oct 2023), Cantina Contest (Nov–Dec 2023); MetaMorpho periphery audited by Spearbit (Nov 2023), OpenZeppelin (Nov 2023), Cantina Contest (Nov–Dec 2023); pre-liquidation periphery audited by Spearbit (Oct 2024), ABDK (Nov 2024); MetaMorpho V1.1 diff audited by Spearbit (Nov 2024), OpenZeppelin (Nov 2024); Public Allocator audited by Spearbit (Mar 2024); Vault V2 audited by Spearbit (May, Aug, Nov 2025), ChainSecurity (Sep 2025), Blackthorn (Sep, Dec 2025), Zellic (Jul 2025), Cantina Contest (Jul 2025), Certora (Dec 2025). Certora formal verification also applied to core and IRM math.

Auditors confirmed to be broadly recognized: Spearbit (tier-1), OpenZeppelin (tier-1), Certora (formal verification specialist), ChainSecurity (recognized), Zellic (recognized), ABDK Consulting (recognized). All firms are on the recognized list in the rubric.

Morpho Blue core (v1.0.0) and Adaptive Curve IRM (v1.0.0) are explicitly described as immutable — no post-deployment code changes are possible for these fund-custody contracts. For Vault V2 (the upgradeable-by-design curator vault layer), audits by Spearbit, ChainSecurity, Zellic, Blackthorn, and Certora were conducted in 2025 covering the currently-deployed codebase. No material drift between audit scope and deployed code is documented; a bytecode diff was not performed in this run.

The Morpho Blue core singleton returns proxy=null from the DeFiPunkd ABI API, confirming it is NOT a proxy — it is a non-upgradeable singleton. There is no implementation contract to separately verify. The ABI source is 'etherscan'. Peripheral contracts (MetaMorpho factories, VaultV2Factory) are factory-deployed clones whose source is verified at the factory level per the docs.

steelman.red: A bytecode diff against the audited commit was not performed in this run; if any peripheral contract (e.g., bundler adapters, vault V2 instances) differs materially from the audited code without a follow-up audit, that constitutes unaudited drift in a fund-path contract.
steelman.orange: Vault V2 is a newer codebase (2025 audits) that is still actively being deployed across many chains; not every chain deployment may have been individually audited, and periphery contracts like migration bundlers were audited against older commits whose exact relationship to current deployed bytecode was not verified this run.
steelman.green: The core Morpho Blue singleton is immutable and verified on Etherscan with ABI sourced from Etherscan (not 'similar match'), it is not a proxy, it is tied to a public GitHub repo at a pinned v1.0.0 tag, and was audited by at least three recognized tier-1 firms (Spearbit, OpenZeppelin, Certora) covering the deployed version. Vault V2 received six separate 2025 audits from recognized firms including Spearbit, ChainSecurity, Zellic, Blackthorn, and Certora formal verification. The docs-to-GitHub linkage is explicit and commit-pinned.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because the core Morpho Blue singleton (the primary fund-custody contract) is verified on Etherscan without proxy wrapping, tied to a public GitHub repo at a pinned v1.0.0 tag, immutable by design, and covered by audits from Spearbit, OpenZeppelin, and Certora at the time of deployment. The Vault V2 layer (MetaMorpho) received six separate 2025 audits from recognized firms. The missing bytecode diff is recorded in unknowns[] as a scope limit per rubric, not a downgrade signal, because the core contract's immutability makes post-audit drift structurally impossible, and the peripheral vault contracts have recent, thorough audit coverage.

evidence.shows: Morpho Blue core singleton (0xBBBBBbbBBb9cC5e90e3b3Af64bdAF62C37EEFFCb) is verified on Etherscan (verified=true, abiSource='etherscan'), is NOT a proxy (proxy=null), and uses the contract name 'Morpho'. ABI contains 28 functions and 17 events matching the published interface.

Morpho Blue core singleton surfacer page confirms ABI source from Etherscan, owner() returns 0xcBa28b38103307Ec8dA98377ffF9816C164f9AFa (DAO governance multisig), feeRecipient() returns zero address, 3 zero-arg view methods pre-executed, contract is not a proxy.

Official Morpho documentation maps every deployed contract to its GitHub source repo and pinned tag or commit SHA (e.g., Morpho Blue core → morpho-blue/tree/v1.0.0, Bundler3 → bundler3/tree/82e44dd..., MetaMorpho V1.1 → 5a0717b2..., pre-liquidation → 16978c5...). Also includes a full audit table listing: Spearbit (Oct 2023 Morpho V1), OpenZeppelin (Oct 2023 Morpho V1), Cantina Contests (Nov–Dec 2023), Spearbit (Nov 2023 MetaMorpho), OpenZeppelin (Nov 2023 MetaMorpho), Spearbit (Oct 2024 pre-liquidation), ABDK (Nov 2024), Spearbit (Nov 2024 MetaMorpho V1.1 diff), OpenZeppelin (Nov 2024 diff), Spearbit (Mar 2024 Public Allocator), and Vault V2 audits by Spearbit, ChainSecurity, Blackthorn, Zellic, Cantina, Certora (multiple rounds, May–Dec 2025).

Morpho security page confirms multi-faceted audit approach including formal verification, mutation tests, fuzzing, unit testing, and peer reviews; references professional security reviews, contests, and pre/post-deployment bounties; full audit list available at get-started/resources/audits/.

Morpho Blue was audited by OpenZeppelin and Spearbit (via Cantina) before launch; followed by a Cantina security contest. Certora formal verification also conducted. Security framework blog post confirms immutability of core contracts and sequence of audits.

unknowns: V2: Independent bytecode diff between deployed contracts and audited GitHub commits was not performed this run; the core Morpho Blue singleton's immutability makes drift structurally impossible for that contract, but peripheral adapters (bundlers, migration adapters) were not individually bytecode-verified

V5: Post-audit drift for Vault V2 peripheral contracts on non-Ethereum chains (e.g., Base, Arbitrum deployments) was not individually verified against audit scope; assumed covered by the same codebase as Ethereum deployments

protocol_metadata.about: Morpho Blue is a decentralized, non-custodial lending protocol on Ethereum and other EVM chains that enables permissionless creation of isolated lending markets, where each market is defined by a loan token, collateral token, oracle, interest rate model, and liquidation LTV. Users can supply assets to earn yield, borrow against collateral, or supply collateral, with liquidation enforced when a position's loan-to-value exceeds the market's LLTV threshold. The core Morpho Blue singleton contract is immutable; on top of it, MetaMorpho vaults (V1) and Vault V2 allow curators to allocate capital across multiple markets using a managed, ERC-4626 compliant vault structure with configurable risk parameters and timelocks.
